sections.html:
Wichita Falls owners can hand the house to a broker, find a private buyer or take a cash bid. How soon you need to move and what the house needs decide which fits. Hail damage, a tired roof or years of skipped upkeep point toward cash. A tidy house can do well on the open market.

Wichita Falls sits in southeast Wichita County on the Wichita River, near the Oklahoma line. It is the county seat and the main population center of the area, so buyers come from across the county and from the Sheppard Air Force Base community. Housing runs from 1920s oil boom homes to postwar and newer houses, and older ones often need updates to wiring, plumbing and foundations. That is where a repair estimate matters most to a buyer.

Before you pick a route, get these done:

  • Sort out the deed, any liens and the mortgage payoff.
  • Collect permit records for roofs, additions and other work.
  • Compare a listing timeline with a cash closing date.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff figure and a list of recorded liens on the property.

The April 10, 1979 tornado cut through the southern part of Wichita Falls, destroyed twenty percent of the dwellings in town and injured more than 3,200 people. Most of the damage was repaired within three years. The memory still shapes how the city treats roofs and other major work.

Wichita Falls requires a city permit for a roof repair over 500 square feet and for any replacement. The contractor must pull it before work starts, and the city expects contractors in town to be bonded and to hold the right credentials.

The city's own notice names resale as a reason to keep permits on file. Future buyers may be wary of major improvements, such as roofing, done without approval. If your roof was replaced after a hail storm, have the permit number and the roofer's invoice ready for the buyer. Unpermitted work can also complicate an insurance claim, and an owner whose roof went in without a permit might find that damage tied to that work is not covered.

A closed permit answers that worry before the buyer raises it. Check any addition, pool or roof from your years of ownership against permit records. A permit that was never closed is worth a call to Building Inspections before you list.

Building Inspections is at 1300 Seventh Street and handles permits and inspections. The city posts forms, checklists and a fee ordinance on its website, and the office phone is 940-761-7459.

Utilities come up in showings. The main water supply is Lake Arrowhead, built in 1966, after earlier reservoirs such as Lake Wichita, Lake Kemp, Lake Diversion and Lake Kickapoo. If a buyer asks about service at a specific address, the city's utility office can answer.

The city gives four reasons to use a permitted job: a bonded contractor, code compliance, safety inspections and insurance coverage. Seller paperwork that shows all four is the quickest way to calm a cautious buyer or lender.

sections.h2: Wichita County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
The Wichita County Tax Office assesses and collects for eight taxing jurisdictions in the county and disburses almost $120 million a year to them. Its website has pages for online payment, penalties and interest, a tax estimator and the list of entities it collects for.

Dates that touch a Wichita Falls sale
DateWhat happens
January 1Values set and tax lien attaches for the year
April 30Most exemption applications due
May 15Last day for most appraisal protests
October 1Bills mailed
January 31Last day to pay without penalty

A title company usually prorates the year's tax between buyer and seller, so ask for the number before you sign. In winter, check the tax office's closure notices before driving over, since it follows the school district's weather announcements.

A school homestead exemption of $140,000, with $60,000 more for owners over 65 or disabled, stays with the owner who qualified. It stops when you sell. A disabled veteran may qualify for larger amounts that rise with the disability rating.

Deeds for Wichita Falls property are recorded by the Wichita County Clerk. The deed needs a signature plus an acknowledgment. Fees are $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per added page.

Foreclosure auctions for a defaulted loan happen on a first Tuesday, once the notice has been up and on file for three weeks. If you close before then, the lender is repaid from the proceeds and the foreclosure can end.

A listing means showings, an inspection and a lender's review, and an open permit or missing invoice can surface at every one of those points. Cash removes the lender, which leaves title work and your payoff as the main clock.

On your side the homework is identical either way. Confirm the deed, request a mortgage payoff, find out about unpaid tax and gather the roof and repair paperwork. Then choose a closing date that fits your move.

With storm damage or an aging roof, ask every buyer who deals with repairs and the permit, and get the offer in writing before committing.

Wichita Falls was platted in July 1876 and incorporated on July 29, 1889. Oil reshaped it. The Electra field opened in 1911 and the Burkburnett fields in 1918, and by 1920 the city had nine refineries. A building boom followed in the early 1920s. Sheppard Field opened in 1941 and became Sheppard Air Force Base in 1948, which brought another round of homebuilding.

The city peaked near 110,100 residents in 1955 and counted 104,197 in 2000. Neighborhoods built from the 1920s through the 1950s sit next to newer subdivisions, and a large mall in the southwest corner of the city pulled retail away from downtown. For a seller, the practical point is age. Older houses mean older roofs, wiring and plumbing, and buyers who finance will ask for inspections that find them.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or a lien owed
sections.html:
Back taxes or a recorded lien will not stop a sale. They come out of your proceeds at closing. Each year's tax lien attaches on January 1, so the title company requests a current figure from the tax office and deducts it from your payout.

Ask the title company early for a payoff on the mortgage and a list of recorded liens. If an old lien was paid but never released, contact whoever holds it for a release before you list, since a release can take time to arrive. A cash buyer can usually work around a messy file faster than a lender can, but the title still has to clear before the deed changes hands.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my roof?
faqs.a: Yes, for a full replacement or a repair over 500 square feet, and the contractor pulls it first. Building Inspections can confirm for a smaller job.
That is the Wichita County Tax Office, which collects for eight taxing jurisdictions. Its website has online payment, a tax estimator and penalty details.

faqs.q: Does the 1979 tornado still matter to Wichita Falls home sellers?
faqs.a: Mostly as building history. The tornado destroyed twenty percent of the city's dwellings, and the city now stresses permits on roofing and other major work. Hold on to repair paperwork.
January 31 is the last day without penalty. From February 1, penalty and interest build, and the year's lien has attached since January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, though buyers and lenders may raise it and some will hesitate. Building Inspections can explain how to close an old permit before you list.
